Modernization is consumer management, not code migration

Legacy data estates fail the same way: undocumented transformations, silent schema drift, weekend crashes with tribal fixes. Modernization is not lifting jobs into the cloud; it is re-contracting them — typed inputs, tested transforms, observable runs, and an owner per pipeline — while the old estate keeps serving under a strangler plan.
The strangler discipline matters more than the target stack: dual-run with output comparison, traffic shifting per consumer, and retirement gates that require evidence, not enthusiasm.
Below: the failure modes that stall migration programs, the reference architecture of the strangler pattern, and the console that tracks parity and retirement honestly.
Four failure modes that stall migration programs
Each of these is organizational gravity — the countermeasures make parity provable and retirement contractual, so the old estate cannot quietly survive.

widgets.title: The lakehouse fabric — click nodes for the contract

nodes.label: Source estates
nodes.detail: Operational DBs, SaaS APIs, event streams — each source carries an ingestion contract: schema, freshness expectation, ownership, PII classification.

nodes.label: Bronze — raw
nodes.detail: Immutable append-only landing with metadata envelopes; reprocessing always possible because nothing is mutated in place.

nodes.label: Schema contracts
nodes.detail: Breaking-change detection at ingestion with producer notification — a source that ships a breaking change learns within minutes.

nodes.label: Silver — conformed
nodes.detail: Validated, deduplicated, typed models with quality gates; the transformation layer is a tested codebase, not a notebook sprawl.

nodes.label: Quality gates
nodes.detail: Row-count anomalies, nullability expectations, referential checks — failures quarantine data with reasons rather than passing silently.

nodes.label: Gold — business
nodes.detail: Dimensional marts and feature tables with documented semantics; the semantic layer from the BI practice reads from here.

nodes.label: Lineage & catalog
nodes.detail: Column-level lineage across the medallion layers — the impact question ('what breaks if this shifts') is answerable from the catalog.

nodes.label: Consumers
nodes.detail: BI, ML features, reverse-ETL and API products — each consumer's SLA inherits from the gold layer's freshness budget.

widgets.note: Click nodes to read the contract each layer carries. The schema contract at ingestion is where reliability is actually won.
